messages:
customer_acct: Hey team — since ~08:00 UTC our API calls are getting routed to eu-west for a subset of ap-south customers. We're seeing +200-300ms tail latency and some 401s that look like a region mismatch. Repro steps below, can someone from infra take a look? :frowning:

anna_support: Sorry you're hitting this — escalating now. Can you paste a failing request id and a curl so SRE can repro?

customer_acct: req_id=rid-8f3a2c. Example:
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'X-Redwood-Region: ap-south' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

anna_support: Thanks. I pulled proxy logs for that req_id and I see upstream cluster = eu-west-gateway even though X-Redwood-Region=ap-south in the request: 
```
[2026-03-17T08:02:13Z] rid-8f3a2c -> upstream cluster: eu-west-gateway, route: /v1/generate, x-redwood-region=ap-south, x-envoy-original-dst-host=api.redwood.ai, response_time_ms=275, status=200
```

sam_sre: @anna_support putting myself on it. Initial hypothesis: a recent L7 route change added a header/host rewrite that causes region-based routing to be bypassed. Checking recent route pushes now. :eyes:

jules_network: I'm seeing a header modifier on the /v1/ route in the latest envoy config snapshot:
```
- match: prefix: /v1/
  route:
    cluster: gateway-cluster
    host_rewrite: eu-west.internal
    request_headers_to_add:
      - header:
          key: x-internal-region
          value: eu-west
```
That host_rewrite + header add would force upstream selection to eu-west for any matching route.

leo_backend: That explains the auth failures — our region selector uses host and x-region hints. If host_rewrite forces eu-west.internal, the selector maps requests to eu-west cluster and tokens signed for ap-south get rejected.

sam_sre: Repro steps I ran from our CI worker:
```
curl -v -H 'X-Redwood-Region: ap-south' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.ai
> X-Redwood-Region: ap-south
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< x-upstream-cluster: eu-west-gateway
```
Expected x-upstream-cluster: ap-south-gateway

ops-bot: Incident created INC-20260317-23 — ENG-ONCALL paged. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/region-routing

sam_sre: Temporary mitigation: toggled runtime flag route_by_region -> false and removed the header_to_add + host_rewrite from the global /v1/ route in the canary config. Rolling to global now; ETA ~20m for full rollout.

anna_support: Noted. Customer notified of mitigation window and asked to validate. I've also flagged Billing — there may be token overage due to cross-region retries.

customer_acct: Thanks — we'll validate after you flip. We saw a ~12% bump in token counts and a few 401s between 08:00-08:20 UTC. Please advise if you need logs.

jules_network: Root cause follow-up: a config intended for a zonal canary included a prefix matcher that accidentally matched the global route (prefix: /v1/ used instead of scoped regex). That allowed the host_rewrite/header add to apply globally. Patch: change matcher to '^/v1/' with zone scoping and add a deploy gate for host_rewrite changes.

sam_sre: Action items: 1) Verify mitigation finish and confirm customer routing restored. 2) Revert any unintended route changes in commit history and add unit test for header preservation when host_rewrite is present. 3) Postmortem and deploy gating for route changes.

anna_support: I'll keep the customer updated and close the support ticket once they confirm. :thumbsup: 

leo_backend: Also plan to add an e2e smoke test that asserts x-upstream-cluster == X-Redwood-Region mapping for reserved customers to catch regressions.

customer_acct: Confirmed at 08:29 UTC — routing back to ap-south, latency normalized, auths fixed. Thanks for the quick action.

sam_sre: Marking INC-20260317-23 resolved -> monitoring for 2 hours. Will open a postmortem doc later.
